summary: Hypertension means the pressure of blood in the arteries stays high. It often causes no symptoms but raises the risk of heart attack, stroke, kidney disease and eye problems over time. It is diagnosed by repeated, correctly measured readings, not by one reading.
symptoms: Very high readings can cause severe headache, chest pain, blurred vision or breathlessness
causes: Often a combination of age, genetics, diet (high salt), weight and inactivity
Sometimes caused by kidney, hormonal or other conditions or by certain medicines

tests.name: Blood pressure measurement (clinic and/or home monitoring)
tests.purpose: Diagnosis is based on repeated readings on different occasions.

preparation.other: Sit and rest quietly for about 5 minutes, avoid caffeine, smoking and exercise for about 30 minutes before, use the correct cuff size and keep the arm at heart level.

tests.exceptions: A single high reading can be due to stress, pain or rushing ('white-coat effect'); the doctor may advise home or 24-hour monitoring.

tests.name: Baseline blood and urine tests (such as blood glucose, kidney function, cholesterol, urine test) and ECG
tests.purpose: Looks for causes and organ effects of high blood pressure.

preparation.fasting: Depends on the test (some cholesterol and glucose tests may need fasting). Follow the lab's instruction.

tests.exceptions: Not every patient needs the same set of tests; the doctor chooses.

prevention: Reduce salt (WHO advises less than 5 g of salt, about one teaspoon, per day)
Eat more vegetables, fruit and pulses
lifestyle: If medicines are prescribed, take them regularly and do not stop on your own even if you feel well
Keep a record of home readings for the doctor
red_flags: Very high reading with severe headache, chest pain, breathlessness, confusion or vision change
Sudden weakness or numbness, face drooping or trouble speaking
In pregnancy: severe headache, visual disturbance, sudden swelling, or pain in the upper abdomen
when_to_consult: Readings that are repeatedly above the normal range
Adults should have their blood pressure checked regularly, even without symptoms
special_populations: Pregnancy: high blood pressure needs prompt obstetric care
Children can also have high blood pressure; use child-appropriate cuffs and see a paediatrician
Older adults need individualised targets set by the doctor

faqs.q: I feel fine. Do I still need to treat high BP?
faqs.a: Yes. High blood pressure usually has no symptoms but still causes damage over time.

faqs.q: Do I have to fast for a BP check?
faqs.a: No. But rest, and avoid caffeine and smoking for about 30 minutes before the reading.
